IDAGIO is the leading streaming service for classical music, based in Berlin and part of IDAGIO Group. The Group spans streaming, recordings, and live music partnerships, globally. Our director initiates projects across all of it: recording partnerships with orchestras, licensing talks with international labels, concert-hall collaborations in Taiwan and Japan, and new ventures.
These initiatives move fast and span many time zones. We are looking for the person at the director's side who keeps them all on track.
Tasks
You are the assistant to the sole director of IDAGIO Group and work with him daily. He travels extensively and meets industry leaders, orchestras, and institutions across Asia, Europe and the US. Every trip produces introductions, ideas, and commitments. Your job is to make sure none of them get lost. You track every thread, follow up with every party, and hold everyone to agreed deadlines, including the director.
Beyond that, you coordinate selected projects across the Group's Berlin companies, working with their Managing Directors. Decisions sit with the director and the Managing Directors. Keeping things moving sits with you.
Assistant and project support to the director
Track and follow up on the projects and partnerships the director runs across the Group. You keep an up-to-date overview of status, owners, and next steps at all times.
Maintain deadlines and flag slipping dates early. You chase open items without being asked.
Prepare agendas, briefings, and follow-ups for meetings. Maintain trackers and status summaries.
Coordinate scheduling, information flow, and documentation across internal and external stakeholders, from orchestra managements to distribution partners.
Project coordination for Moto Lab
Moto Lab Partners is the Group's newest venture: it supports classical artists and institutions in building their international presence and careers, from recordings and concert videos to release strategy and promotion.
Coordinate Moto Lab's projects from start to finish, whatever their shape: a release, a concert video production, a marketing campaign, or a partner engagement.
Act as the central point of contact between everyone involved: artists and their management, orchestras, production crews, distributors, agencies, and internal teams.
Track each project's timeline from planning through delivery, follow up on deliverables, and support project and budget administration until everything is complete and approved.

Several years of professional experience, typically 2 to 5, in an assistant, coordination, project management, or artist management role. This should not be your first job. You have managed deadlines across multiple stakeholders and worked alongside a demanding senior principal before.
A firm understanding of classical music and the industry around it: repertoire, orchestras, how recordings and releases work. A background in classical music (studies, an orchestra, a label, an agency, a concert hall) is a strong plus.
Proactive and organized by temperament. You take ownership, chase without being prompted, and flag problems early.
Comfortable running several projects in parallel and prioritizing against deadlines.
Clear, structured communication and documentation. Status is transparent to everyone at any time.
Fluent German and English (C1 or better, spoken and written). Japanese or Mandarin is a real plus given our partners in Japan and Taiwan.
Based in Berlin or willing to relocate. Occasional flexibility for calls with Asia or the US and for concert or recording dates in the evening.

A rare vantage point: you work directly with the director of a music group active between Europe and Asia, and you see every initiative across it.
Real responsibility from day one. The role exists because these projects matter and need an owner.
A small, senior, international team in Berlin with short decision paths.
Salary range: €42,000–50,000 gross/year, depending on experience.
Send a short cover note, your CV, and your earliest possible start date to apply. Tell us about one person or project you supported where your follow-through made the difference.
IDAGIO and the IDAGIO Group value diversity. We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet 100% of the requirements.

Pour notre division **Systèmes d'information**, nous recherchons un **Responsable de projets (H/F)** dont la mission principale sera de piloter la mise en oeuvre de projets depuis l'expression du besoin jusqu'au déploiement et au suivi opérationnel.
## *Responsabilités* ##
* Conduire, optimiser et être garant de l'ensemble des ressources du projet/ programme (humains, budget, clientèle, décision finale)
* Diriger la gestion financière du projet ainsi que de toutes les exigences définies (qualité, coût, délai...)
* Assumer l'alignement du projet/ programme aux besoins des métiers
* Organiser, coordonner et animer l'équipe projet/ programme
* Arbitrer les éventuels différends entre l'équipe et les autres intervenants
* Superviser le déroulement du projet
* Coordonner, synthétiser et assurer la qualité des validations prononcées
* Gérer la relation avec les fournisseurs
## *Profil* ##
* Diplôme d'une école d'Ingénieur (Master HES ou EPF)
* Expérience de 3 à 5 ans en gestion de projets, idéalement dans un environnement industriel exigeant
* Expérience dans la conduite de projets s'appuyant sur des pratiques et/ ou méthodes Agiles
* De langue maternelle française avec des bonnes connaissances d'anglais
* Bonne maîtrise des outils et systèmes informatiques
* Maîtrise avérée des approches prédictives et Agiles, ainsi que des outils de gestion de projet
* Rigoureux, autonome, organisé et doté d-un fort sens des responsabilités
* Excellentes capacités d-analyse et de synthèse
* Capacité à adapter l-approche de pilotage au contexte, aux enjeux et au niveau de maturité des équipes
* Esprit d-ouverture et goût du travail en équipe
* Très bonnes aptitudes en communication, leadership naturel et sens du service client

s.h: Duties listed below are at the Full Performance level- GS-15.
s.t:
Serves as a technical expert and coordinator in providing intellectual leadership and focus on the unit’s research.
Incumbent assesses the impact of substantive programs and policies-including legislation, new USDA and FS policy, and State and private sector policies related to forestry research and resource management-on assigned projects.
Selects and promulgates research priorities based upon the program area(s) assigned and Station guidelines.
Determines most economical means of meeting the Program and Station objectives within fiscal and legal constraints and takes action to ensure these means are followed.
Submits and justifies requests for major expenditures to higher levels of leadership.
The incumbent monitors and evaluates the quality and effectiveness of the assigned research program.

s.h: Supervisory Responsibilities 25% or more of the time.
s.t:
In order to qualify, you must meet the eligibility and qualifications requirements as defined below by the closing date of the announcement. For more information on the qualifications for this position, visit the Office of Personnel Management's General Schedule Qualification Standards.

Your application and resume must clearly show that you possess the experience requirements. Transcripts must be provided for qualifications based on education. Provide course descriptions as necessary. This is an interdisciplinary position and may be filled in any of the job series listed below.

Basic Requirement: GS-0101 Series: Degree: Successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree that included a major field of study in behavioral or social science; or related disciplines appropriate to the position.

OR Combination of education and experience -- that provided the applicant with knowledge of one or more of the behavioral or social sciences equivalent to a major in the field.

OR Four years of appropriate experience that demonstrated that the applicant has acquired knowledge of one or more of the behavioral or social sciences equivalent to a major in the field.

GS-0110 Series: Degree: Successfully completed a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree that included a major field of study in economics, that included at least 21 semester hours in economics and 3 semester hours in statistics, accounting, or calculus.

OR Combination of education and experience that included 24 semester hours in course work equivalent to a major in economics, as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education sufficient to demonstrate that I possess the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform work in the occupation that is comparable to that normally acquired through the successful completion of a full 4-year course of study with a major in the appropriate field needed to perform the work of the occupation.

Examples of appropriate experience to qualify in the Economics series include: Individual economic research assignments requiring planning, information assembly, analysis and evaluation, conclusions and report preparation; Supervisory or project coordination assignments involving a staff of professional economists, and requiring the evaluation and interpretation of economic information; OR Teaching assignments in a college or university that included both class instruction in economics subjects and one of the following: (1) personal research that produced evidence of results, (2) direction of graduate theses in economics, or (3) service as a consultant or advisor on technical economics problems.

Basic Requirements: GS-0401 Series: Degree: Successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree that included a major field of study in biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry, or related disciplines appropriate to the position.

OR A bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in a major field of study that included 24 semester hours in course work in biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry, or related disciplines appropriate to the position.

Related course work generally refers to courses that may be accepted as part of the program major.

OR A combination of education and experience that included 24 semester hours in course work in biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry or related disciplines appropriate to the position, AND experience sufficient to demonstrate that I possess the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform work in the occupation that is comparable to that normally acquired through the successful completion of a full 4-year course of study with a major in the appropriate field needed to perform the work of the position.

In addition to meeting the basic requirement, you must also possess experience and/or directly related education in the amounts listed below. Specialized Experience Requirement: For the GS-14 level: Applicants must have one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 in the Federal service.

Qualifying specialized experience is defined as three or more of the following: Applies knowledge of natural resources research practices and techniques to convey information concerning scientific topics, policies, and programs to key publics with diverse levels of understanding of scientific disciplines, programs and activities Initiates high priority special projects, studies, and initiatives that affect critical aspects of organizational programs.

Implements natural resource programs and projects including programming, budgeting, and administering the organization's program of work. Provides advice, briefings, assistance and counsel to leadership on responding to the media and/or congressional staff on scientific topics and program activities.

For the GS-15 level: Applicants must have one year specialized experience equivalent to the GS-14 in the Federal service.

Qualifying specialized experience is defined as all of the following: Applies knowledge of natural resources research practices and techniques to convey information concerning scientific topics, policies, and programs to key publics with diverse levels of understanding of scientific disciplines, programs and activities.

Develops and directs short and long-range programs and projects including programming, budgeting, and administering the organization's program of work. Reviews scientific research findings and makes recommendations to improve to a natural resources program's content, and methods of investigating research problems.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

TIME IN GRADE REQUIREMENT: If you are a current federal employee in the General Schedule (GS) pay plan and applying for a promotion opportunity, you must meet time-in-grade (TIG) requirements of 52 weeks of service at the next lower grade level in the normal line of progression for the position being filled.

This requirement must be met by the closing date of this announcement.

The Department of Energy's mission is to ensure America's security and prosperity by addressing its energy, environmental and nuclear challenges through transformative science and technology solutions.

The Office of the Chief Information Officer is responsible for advancing the Department's missions through policy, standards, and services that meet mission requirements, balance risk and innovation, and set clear performance goals and expectations for the enterprise information ecosystem.

We are truly honored that DOE has been named America's #1 Best Employer for Veterans in 2023 by Forbes-not only among Government agencies, but among employers across the U.S. We are so proud of this ranking which reflects our commitment to the employment of veterans.

As so many veterans at DOE renew their service to our Nation, we are deeply committed to their success and advancement.

Veterans shape the future of energy As a Supervisory IT Program Manager, you will: Forms and executes strategic security policies and acts as the deciding authority for evaluating and approving security packages for high-impact unclassified and classified (up to Top Secret/SCI) national security systems.

Provides executive leadership over security assessments, independent audits, and compliance reviews to identify system vulnerabilities, track plan of action and milestones (POA&Ms), and ensure federal data privacy rules are met.

Plans, directs, and standardizes cybersecurity training and awareness campaigns across the agency, ensuring critical leadership roles and authorizing officials receive required training.

Formulates long-range workforce plans, strategically forecasts future technological skill needs, and partners with Human Resources to recruit and hire highly cleared cybersecurity specialists.

Works directly with senior Department leadership (such as the CIO and CISO) and represents the agency in high-level interagency working groups to align cybersecurity policy across federal portfolios.

Manages day-to-day office operations by planning and assigning work, setting priorities, developing performance standards, assessing employee performance, and identifying training needs for subordinates.
You must meet both the Basic Requirement and the Specialized Experience to qualify for this series as described below. BASIC REQUIREMENT Applicants must have IT-related education and experience demonstrating each of the four competencies listed below at a proficiency level equivalent to the next lower grade level in federal service.

Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail.

Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services.

Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately.

Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations.

SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS: A qualified candidate's online application and resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-14 in the Federal service.

Specialized experience for this position is defined as meeting ALL of the following: Serving as a senior lead directing Risk Management Framework (RMF) or security assessment and authorization (A&A) processes, and developing organization-wide cybersecurity policies, plans, or compliance standards for complex systems.; managing complex cybersecurity projects or portfolios, which includes allocating budgets, determining resource requirements, and managing the performance of multi-disciplinary teams.

Designing, planning, and administering large-scale cybersecurity training, security awareness, or professional workforce development programs to identify and close critical technical skill gaps across a large organization. "Experience" refers to paid and unpaid experience.

Examples of qualifying unpaid experience may include: volunteer work done through National Service programs (such as Peace Corps and AmeriCorps); as well as work for other community-based philanthropic and social organizations.

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills; and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Limit your resume to no more than two (2) pages.

If more than two pages are submitted, only the first two pages will be reviewed to determine your eligibility and qualifications. Your full resume will be made available to the hiring manager if you are referred.

Time-in-Grade: Current Federal employees must meet time-in-grade requirements by the closing date of this announcement to receive consideration and current employees must have at least a fully successful or equivalent performance rating to receive consideration.

You must meet all qualifications and eligibility requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

Arcadia is dedicated to happier, healthier days for all. We believe that there is a better healthcare world – one powered by data. Our platform transforms complex, diverse data into a unified foundation for health, helping organizations deliver better care, boost revenue, and lower costs.
We’re a team of fiercely driven individuals committed to making healthcare more sustainable—and we’re looking for passionate people to help us get there.
For more information, visit .
Why This Role Is Important to Arcadia
At Arcadia , the Enterprise Implementation Manager (EIM) is the customer's primary point of accountability from contract signature through the life of the relationship.

The EIM manages a portfolio of enterprise accounts, leading each customer through onboarding and the technical work required to bring them live — including project managing new data connector builds — but the role exists to protect and grow the value the customer realizes from Arcadia 's platform.

EIMs proactively build the client relationship, drive adoption, resolve risk before it threatens retention, and act as the customer's trusted advisor long after go-live, ensuring customer value is clearly tracked & regularly reviewed.
The ideal candidate is a relationship-first operator: someone who can run a technical delivery workstream competently, but who is just as comfortable owning a client conversation, coaching a teammate, or spotting an account risk before it becomes a retention problem.
What Success Looks Like
In 3 months
Complete onboarding and current product and enablement certifications; build a working understanding of the platform, data model, and Arcadia 's customer success playbooks. The optional Arcadia Certified Professional program is available for continued growth. Shadow tactical client touchpoints and status conversations to learn how EIMs build trust and manage expectations across a client relationship
Take ownership of a defined workstream — for example, project managing a new data connector build — with support from your manager and technical partners
In 6 months
Independently manage cross-team workflows (data integration, configuration, connector builds) while keeping priorities visible and surfacing risk early
Lead tactical client conversations and standing touchpoints, delivering clear, timely updates that keep stakeholders aligned and confident
Proactively identify and escalate delivery or account risk, applying established playbooks to resolve issues efficiently and maintain momentum
Begin building trusted relationships with client stakeholders, understanding their unique technical and business priorities
Contribute to Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs), Executive Business Reviews (EBRs), or steering committees for your accounts, and become fluent in maintaining account health scores in Planhat
Build fluency with Arcadia 's customer feedback channels, including the Customer Satisfaction Score (CSAT), as part of engaging your accounts
In 12 months
Own a portfolio of enterprise accounts as the primary point of contact — coordinating delivery, connector project management, and ongoing value acceleration & account health under one roof
Drive accountability for on-time, high-quality delivery of commitments, from new data connector implementations to platform adoption milestones
Independently lead recurring QBRs, EBRs, or steering committees, and own the Planhat health score and NPS trajectory for your portfolio, working toward a consistently green status
Partner effectively with the Customer Growth and Retention (CGR) team on renewal and expansion conversations, providing account context and continuity while CGR owns the commercial process
Identify and document process or value improvements, contributing refinements that strengthen delivery consistency and customer outcomes
Share lessons learned and best practices with peers, informally mentoring newer EIMs and Project Associates
What You'll Be Doing
Customer Relationship & Trust
Own a portfolio of enterprise accounts, serving as the customer's primary point of contact throughout the engagement.
Lead tactical status conversations and standing project meetings, delivering clear, timely updates on progress, risk, and next steps.
Facilitate regular touchpoints to align priorities, answer client questions, and maintain stakeholder trust.
Prepare accurate, client-ready documentation and materials that support transparent communication.
Account Health & Governance
Serve as the customer's primary point of accountability for delivery outcomes and overall account health across your portfolio.
Lead recurring QBRs, EBRs, or steering committees with client leadership, tying progress to shared goals, ROI, and next steps.
Maintain each account's health score in Planhat, incorporating usage, engagement, and other signals; own the goal of moving accounts toward a consistently green status. Contribute to your segment's (Core, Enterprise, or National) Net Promoter Score (NPS), which factors into incentive compensation at the segment level rather than by individual account.
Build fluency with Arcadia 's customer feedback channels — including CSAT — as part of the company's growing Voice-of-Customer program.
Partner with the CGR team on renewal and expansion conversations, providing account context, continuity, and delivery insight; CGR owns the commercial renewal and upsell process.
Proactively identify and escalate delivery and account risk; apply established playbooks to resolve issues efficiently.
Maintain project and account momentum through consistent follow-through and clear ownership of open items.
Drive accountability for commitments by managing dependencies and communicating progress across all workstreams.
Implementation & Data Connector Project Management
Project-manage new data connector builds and platform configuration workstreams from kickoff through validation and go-live.
Ensure smooth data orchestration through configuration validation, and maintain detailed documentation of process flows and integrations.
Partner cross-functionally with Data & Health Platform (DHP) teams and engineering to resolve data alignment issues and strengthen reporting reliability.
Cross-Functional Coordination
Manage workflows to maintain alignment and efficiency across internal teams, third parties, and the client.
Coordinate delivery activities and track interdependencies so priorities stay visible and risks surface early.
Ensure project team collaboration and escalate promptly if a workstream is tracking behind.
Value Realization & Continuous Improvement

Contribute to continuous improvement by sharing refinements and strengthening knowledge capture across projects.
Connect delivery and account activities to the customer's broader adoption and value-realization goals.

Share lessons learned and best practices from client engagements with peers and newer team members.
Apply feedback to continuously refine your own skills and performance, modeling a growth mindset for the team.

Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. English Language Proficiency: Psychologists must be proficient in spoken and written English in accordance with VA Handbook 5005, Part II, Chapter 3, section A, paragraph 3j.

Education: Have a doctoral degree in psychology from a graduate program in psychology accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA), the Psychological Clinical Science Accreditation System (PCSAS), or the Canadian Psychological Association (CPA) at the time the program was completed.

The specialty area of the degree must be consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed. For the purpose of meeting this requirement, the term "specialty area" refers to the specific specialty areas recognized by the accrediting body and not to specific job duties that might require special skills.

Currently, APA accredits doctoral programs in the specialty areas of clinical psychology, counseling psychology, school psychology, or combinations of two or more of those areas. PCSAS accredits doctoral programs in psychological clinical science.

CPA accredits doctoral programs in clinical psychology, counseling psychology, clinical neuropsychology, and school psychology. There are no job assignments in VHA that require the skills of a school psychologist; therefore, an applicant with a degree in the specialty area of school psychology is not eligible for appointment.

Strictly for the purpose of determining eligibility for appointment as a psychologist in VHA, there is no distinction between the specialty areas (with the exception of school psychology).

OR Have a doctoral degree in any area of psychology and, in addition, successfully complete a re-specialization program (including documentation of an approved internship completed as part of the re-specialization program) meeting both of the following conditions: The re-specialization program must be completed in an APA or a CPA accredited doctoral program; and The specialty in which the applicant is retrained must be consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

NOTE: The applicant must provide an official transcript and/or certificate documenting the completion of the re-specialization program, which includes completion of an APA or CPA internship. OR Have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally-accredited institution, with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature.

AND Internship: Have successfully completed a professional psychology internship training program that was accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed and that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

OR New VHA psychology internship programs that are in the process of applying for APA accreditation are acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement, provided that such programs were sanctioned by the VHA Central Office Program Director for Psychology and the VHA Office of Academic Affiliations at the time that the individual was an intern.

OR VHA facilities that offered full-time, one-year pre-doctoral internships prior to PL 96-151 (pre-1979) are considered to be acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement.

OR Applicants who completed an internship that was not accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed may be considered eligible for hire only if they are currently board certified by the American Board of Professional Psychology in a specialty area that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

(NOTE: Once board certified, the employee is required to maintain board certification.) OR Applicants who have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally-accredited institution with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature may fulfill this internship requirement by having the equivalent of a one-year supervised internship experience in a site specifically acceptable to the candidate's doctoral program.

If the internship experience is not noted on the applicant's official transcript, the applicant must provide a statement from the doctoral program verifying that the equivalent of a one-year supervised internship experience was completed in a site acceptable to the doctoral program.

Licensure: Hold a full, current, and unrestricted license to practice psychology at the doctoral level in a State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States, or the District of Columbia.

May qualify based on being covered by the Grandfathering Provision as described in the VA Qualification Standard for this occupation (only applicable to current VHA employees who are in this occupation and meet the criteria).

Reiche deine Bewerbungsunterlagen online über unser Jobportal ein. Damit wir deine Unterlagen weiterbearbeiten können, musst du ein Login erstellen. JUUL Labs is seeking a multifunctional Manufacturing Operations Program Manager to join our Global Supply Chain team. This hybrid role bridges day-to-day contract manufacturing execution with strategic, end-to-end supply chain management.
The mission of this role is to ensure we build products at the right speed (time to market), right price (fully burdened cost), right capacity, and right flexibility to meet the company's growth needs. Time to Market & Operational Execution

Cost Management & Financial Acumen
Fully Burdened Cost Tracking: Manage total product supply chain costs to ensure the fully burdened price (including material, labor, overhead, and logistics) directly aligns with corporate profitability margins.
Should-Cost Strategy: Partner with finance and engineering to build aggressive should-costs and clear capital expenditure forecasts.
Commercial Negotiations: Negotiate with key suppliers to secure favorable pricing, tooling/equipment budgets, and business terms without compromising product quality.
Capacity Planning, Flexibility & Scalability
Constraint Mitigation: Evaluate production constraints and manage global manufacturing capacity to seamlessly support current volumes and future product roadmaps.
Ramp & Scale Planning: Collaborate with manufacturing partners on staffing, facility foot printing, and equipment allocation to ensure infrastructure is scalable for company growth.
Adaptability: Implement flexible supply chain strategies capable of responding rapidly to market fluctuations, operational bottlenecks, and demand shifts.
Supplier Relationship & Risk Management
Strategic Alignment: Build, evaluate, and maintain relationships with critical contract manufacturers and component vendors to align them with JUUL's operational targets.
Contingency Planning: Anticipate vulnerabilities and draft proactive business continuity plans to mitigate risks associated with vendor performance, geopolitical fluctuations, and macro supply disruptions.
Performance Quality: Establish metric scorecards and Clear to Build (CTB) tracking to eliminate post-ramp qualifications and unexpected disruptions.
Cross-Functional Leadership & Continuous Improvement
Primary Liaison: Act as the primary champion and operational advocate across engineering, quality, product management, logistics, and finance.
Process Excellence: Utilize KPIs to actively monitor supply chain performance, using a data-driven "sixth sense" to spark continuous improvement, process modifications, and cost-saving loops.

Leadership & Influence: Proven history of leading and influencing cross-functional matrixed teams and external partners toward aggressive timelines without relying on direct authority.
Strategic Problem Solving: Advanced capability to switch focus between minute operational issues and high-level macro strategies; a self-starter who proactively hunts for issues and implements permanent solutions.
Technical & Cost Knowledge: Deep comprehension of manufacturing cost structures, automation equipment, and design principles, including basic DFMAC (Design for Manufacturing/Assembly/Cost) metrics.
Systems Proficiency: Highly proficient with standard enterprise software alongside solid familiarity with ERP and supply chain management systems.
Communication Style: Outstanding verbal and written presentation skills with the poise to navigate complex commercial discussions and articulate clear status reports to executives.
Global Travel: Open to traveling globally between 5% and 10% as required.

About Wolt
At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we’re building the delivery of (almost) everything and you’ll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.
Working at Wolt isn’t always easy, but it’s definitely exciting. Here you’ll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You’ll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you’re a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

Every contact that reaches a customer support agent, and every credit issued to customers, represents a defect somewhere in our system. This role exists to help find those defects, trace them to their source, and work with the teams responsible to eliminate them at a systemic level.
This is a high impact senior program management role within the EMEA Customer Experience organisation, reporting to the Director of Defect Elimination and Customer Experience. The Senior Program Manager is accountable for turning customer experience signals from Wolt and/or Deliveroo markets into clear, actionable insight, and for driving the resulting fixes through to resolution with partner teams.
What you’ll be doing
You will own the delivery of the defect elimination program across EMEA, including application of the defect driver taxonomy to identify where defect rate concentrates, and where customer outcomes are worst. You will build a clear, prioritised list of issues for partner teams to work through.
You will represent the voice of the customer in the rooms where decisions get made about your markets. That means preparing and presenting data in product reviews, weekly/monthly business reviews and planning sessions, so the cost of poor customer experience is concrete and attributable, and so partner teams understand what is being asked of them and why.
You will build working relationships with partner teams in engineering, marketplace operations, courier operations, and finance, and you will track the fixes they commit to through to completion. You will feed results back into the program so everyone can see what worked, and to ensure defects are eliminated for good.
You will maintain and improve the data infrastructure and reporting that underpins this work, ensuring customer experience insights are credible, available and actionable.
Our humble expectations
The right person for this role has spent time inside a large-scale customer experience or operations function, and has direct experience translating customer defects through identification, root cause analysis and resolution. They are comfortable working with imperfect data, and they know how to build a credible case when the evidence is directional rather than conclusive.
Strong analytical instincts are essential. This person needs to know what questions to ask of the data and whether the answers make sense. Prior exposure to a successful voice of the customer (VoC) program is critical.
There is a meaningful cross-functional dimension to the role. This person will spend real time getting other teams to prioritise work that benefits the customer but may compete with other priorities. That requires good judgement, clear communication, and the ability to build trust quickly with people outside their reporting line.
The role also requires the ability to drive results in a dynamic and ambiguous landscape. The right person will combine introducing structure and rigor, while being agile and responsive to changing priorities and emerging issues.
This is a high impact and high visibility role, with the opportunity to interact with stakeholders and teams across the full customer lifecycle. The role will also span across 40 EMEA Roo & Wolt markets, meaning there is an opportunity to drive financial and customer experience results at scale.
Next steps
You will first meet with our Talent Acquisition team to understand role and company fit. Then, you will meet with the Hiring Manager who will talk through your relevant experience and ask you competency based questions that assess your suitability for the role.

The third stage is an assignment, where you will be given a business problem to think through, and present back to the team. If successful, there may be a final conversation with a more senior stakeholder. Throughout all stages, you will have plenty of opportunities to ask any questions about the role, team or company.
Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion
We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

Junior Projektleiter Engineering
Über die Position
Als Junior Projektleiter Engineering wirst du eigenständig technische Neu\- und Umbauprojekte sowie Prozessoptimierungen direkt am Produktionsstandort in Istighofen mitleiten, koordinieren und umsetzen.
Deine Aufgaben
Technische Projektleitung von A bis Z: Du verantwortest Neu\- und Umbauprojekte von Anlagen, Systemen oder Baugruppen am Standort Istighofen von der ersten Idee über die Ausschreibung und Realisierung bis hin zur finalen Abschlusskontrolle hinsichtlich Leistung, Qualität, Terminen und Budget.
Prozessoptimierung in der Produktion: Du analysierst die bestehenden Fertigungs\- und Geschäftsprozesse vor Ort und entwickelst konkrete Massnahmen, um die Anlagenverfügbarkeit, die Energieeffizienz sowie die Produktqualität zu steigern.
Anlagen\-Digitalisierung: Du arbeitest eng mit dem Data Engineer zusammen, um die Produktionsanlagen technisch anzubinden, Datenströme für die Überwachung aufzusetzen und digitale Steuerungen einzurichten.
Instandhaltung und Infrastruktur: Du unterstützt den Betriebsleiter organisatorisch bei der Wartung der Werkshalle sowie der technischen Infrastruktur und hilfst dabei, die Arbeitssicherheit im Betrieb zu gewährleisten.
Ergebnisse präsentieren und Teams abholen: Du bereitest Projektschritte und technische Veränderungen verständlich auf, präsentierst diese vor der Betriebsleitung sowie den Werkstatt\-Teams und nimmst die operativen Mitarbeiter vor Ort direkt bei den Neuerungen mit.
Must\-Haves
Macher\-Mindset mit hoher Energie: Du hast eine hohe Affinität und Leidenschaft für technische Fragestellungen, denkst in Sprints und agierst als Initiator, um neue Projekte eigenständig anzustossen.
Brückenbauer\-Qualitäten: Du besitzt die Empathie, um die Werksmitarbeiter in einfacher Sprache abzuholen und mitzunehmen. Du bist emotional belastbar und verstehst es, dass Veränderungsvorschläge in der Produktion anfangs als Kritik aufgefasst werden können.

Erste Praxis: Erste Erfahrung im Produktionsumfeld ist von Vorteil, sei es durch ein Praktikum, ein Projekt oder eine Ausbildung.
Sprache: Fliessendes Hochdeutsch.
Nice\-to\-have
Auto \& Führerschein: Von Vorteil für den Arbeitsweg, da der Standort nicht optimal angebunden ist.

Dabei musst du nicht bereits alles können. Viel wichtiger sind dein Interesse an der Baubranche, deine strukturierte Arbeitsweise und deine Bereitschaft, dich fachlich weiterzuentwickeln.

Du unterstützt unsere Gesamt\- und Projektleitungen bei der organisatorischen und administrativen Abwicklung unserer Bauprojekte.

* Nachführen von Projektinformationen und Dokumentationen
* Vorbereitung von Sitzungen, Besprechungen und Entscheidungsgrundlagen
* Koordination und Nachverfolgung von offenen Punkten
* Unterstützung der Projektleitung bei organisatorischen und administrativen Themen
* Zusammenarbeit mit Architekt:innen, Ingenieur:innen, Bauleitungen, Unternehmern und weiteren Projektbeteiligten
Mit zunehmender Erfahrung übernimmst du selbstständig anspruchsvollere Aufgaben in den Bereichen **Kosten, Submission und Bauadministration**.
Das bringst du mit
Du hast eine **kaufmännische oder vergleichbare Ausbildung** und idealerweise bereits Erfahrung in der Baubranche.

s.t:

Zudem wirken Sie an öffentlichkeitswirksamen Dokumentationen mit, beauftragen Evaluationen und Expertisen und fördern den Wissenstransfer zwischen Praxis, Fachwelt und Öffentlichkeit.
Für diese Aufgabe bringen Sie mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Projektförderung mit, idealerweise im Schweizer Stiftungs-, Gesundheits- oder Sozialwesen oder in der Zusammenarbeit mit Förderstiftungen. Sie verfügen über einen Hochschul- oder Fachhochschulabschluss im Bereich Sozialwissenschaften oder über eine vergleichbare Qualifikation.

Fragestellungen rund ums Älterwerden sind Ihnen vertraut; zudem arbeiten Sie sich rasch in neue Themenfelder ein. Persönlich überzeugen Sie durch Empathie, Humor, systemisches Denken sowie eine vernetzte, sorgfältige und lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise.
Es erwartet Sie eine sinnstiftende Tätigkeit mit hohem gesellschaftlichem Wirkungsgrad, ein angenehmes Arbeitsklima in einem kleinen Team sowie gute und flexible Arbeitsbedingungen. Wir freuen uns auf Ihre vollständigen Bewerbungsunterlagen.
